:::{#def-half-space}
#### Open half-space

Let $\mathcal{H} = \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b = 0}$ be a hyperplane (@def-hyperplane).
The two **open half-spaces**
[@wikipedia_half_space_geometry]
of $\mathcal{H}$ are

$$
\mathcal{H}^+ \eqdef \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b > 0}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\mathcal{H}^- \eqdef \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b < 0}.
$$ {#eq-half-space}

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-closed-half-space}
#### Closed half-space

The **closed half-spaces** of the hyperplane $\mathcal{H}$ of @def-half-space also include $\mathcal{H}$ itself:
$\mathcal{H}^+ \cup \mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^- \cup \mathcal{H}$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}
Replacing $(\vec{w}, b)$ by $(-\vec{w}, -b)$ describes the same hyperplane
but swaps the names $\mathcal{H}^+$ and $\mathcal{H}^-$.
The sign of $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b$ tells you which side of the hyperplane $\vx$ is on.
A linear classifier uses this sign to assign one of two labels.
:::
